adaptation_framework.task: AI prompts teacher request for activity examples and modifications according to child ability level
adaptation_framework.output: *Adaptation: Let me know if you would like more examples to use in an activity or whether you would like me to increase or decrease the level of difficulty of an activity. Please specify whether the activity is in the Review & Connect, Model Explain Engage, Guided Practice, or Application part of the lesson.

activity_examples.task: Respond to teacher request to provide multiple examples to use for the writing activity
activity_examples.output: Provide detailed examples that teachers could use in their writing activity

example.input: Teacher requests more examples FOR 'What Conflict Can Come From This Setting?' activity

output.title: Here are some examples to use for the 'What Conflict Can Come From This Setting?' activity

icy_land.name: Icy Land (Arctic / Snowy Mountains)
conflicts: A snowstorm makes it hard to find the way home.
An animal slips on the ice and gets separated from its family.
A character's shelter collapses under heavy snow.
A character's hands are too cold to open their supply bag.
The frozen ground cracks beneath their feet.

stormy_sea.name: Stormy Sea
conflicts: A boat gets caught in huge waves and begins to tip.
The wind blows away the map needed to find land.
Lightning strikes near the boat and breaks the mast.
A character falls overboard and needs rescue.
A storm washes a treasure chest into the deep ocean.

hot_desert.name: Hot Desert
conflicts: A character runs out of water and gets very thirsty.
A sandstorm covers the footprints that show the way back.
A snake or scorpion blocks the path.
The sun is so hot the character has to find shade fast.
The character's backpack breaks and they lose supplies.

busy_city.name: Busy City
conflicts: A child gets separated from their adult in a crowd.
A pet escapes its leash and runs into traffic.
A character loses their money and can't get on the bus.
Loud noises scare a small child or animal.
A character's phone dies and they can't contact anyone.

deep_forest.name: Deep Forest
conflicts: It gets dark and the character forgets a flashlight.
A bridge over a river breaks, and they must find another way.
A bear is blocking the path to camp.
A character drops their compass and gets lost.
Their food gets taken by a raccoon while they sleep.

ability_level_modifications.task: Respond to teacher request for a modified teacher script in which the activity is modified according to teacher request of Low, Middle, or High child level ability
ability_level_modifications.output: Revise lesson plan with modified teacher script of activity

guidance.modification_principles: To modify any activity, break the task down further into its component parts, according to theories of working and long-term memory. USE FORM Z for guidance to modify
guidance.alternative_approach: Additionally, you could modify the activity by changing the activity to a lower level. Use FORM P for a list of suggested activities by ability level: Low, Middle, or High.
guidance.reference: Use FORM P for guidance in instruction and possible activities to use during the lesson

example.input: teacher requests a modification to increase the difficulty of the Relevant vs. Irrelevant Match activity (low level)

teacher_script: {Teacher points to the sentence on the board.} 'Let's read this topic sentence together: Penguins' bodies help them survive the cold.' {Teacher models reading it aloud.} 'That's our main idea. Let's look at some details. I'll read one and you decide—does it match the main idea? Give me a thumbs up if yes, thumbs down if no, and flat if you're not sure.'
{Teacher reads: 'Penguins have a thick layer of blubber under the skin.'} 'Thumbs?' (Children show thumbs up) 'Yes! That supports our main idea. It tells us how their body keeps them warm.'

{Teacher reads: 'Penguins eat krill and fish.'} 'Thumbs?' (Children show thumbs down or flat) 'Right. It's about penguins, but not about how their bodies help them survive the cold. Let's set that one aside.'
{Teacher reads: 'Their feathers are waterproof and trap warm air.'} 'Thumbs?' (Children show thumbs up) 'Great! That's a match. It tells us more about how their bodies keep them warm.'

{Teacher reads: 'Penguins live in southern places like the Antarctic.'} 'Thumbs?' (Children show thumbs down or flat) 'Good thinking. This one is true, but not about their bodies helping with the cold.'
{Teacher gestures to the board.} 'Now let's take the matching ones and put them underneath our topic sentence. That helps us stay focused and give strong support for our idea.'
